subject: Landing plan & milestone-linked commit schedule for Atlas AI evaluation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@atlas.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Landing plan & milestone-linked commit schedule for Atlas AI evaluation

Laura —

Great to speak this morning. As discussed, I pulled together a compact landing plan that ties the evaluation milestones to a pragmatic commit/ramp schedule so Atlas can lock predictable economics as you scale tests. The goal is to keep your evaluation fast (2–3 weeks of heavy usage per phase) while giving you optionality on commit volume and predictable pricing as you cross milestones.

High level:
- Phase 0 (POC): 0 committed tokens, limited test access for 2 weeks to validate latency/quality.
- Phase 1 (Eval Pilot): optional light commit (100k tokens/mo) during a 4-week pilot to stabilize latency and usage patterns.
- Phase 2 (Initial Ramp): commit to 500k tokens/mo for months 1–3 after pilot completion; applies 10% list discount.
- Phase 3 (Scale): tiered commits by month after month 3 (1M -> 2M tokens/mo) with additional volume discounts and priority capacity.

I've attached a first draft MAP (Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf) and a simple pricing grid (redwood_pricing_grid_q1.csv) that maps commit bands to discounts and SLA tiers. Can you confirm:
1) The two-week cadence for Phase 0 and 4-week pilot cadence for Phase 1 work for your PMs?
2) Do you want the Phase 1 commit to be mandatory to access caching/priority lanes, or keep it optional and simply recommended?
3) Who from procurement should I copy on the next email — I'll include a minimal SOW and the pricing table for redlines.

If that timeline looks good, I’ll loop Marissa to finalize the discount trigger language tied to monthly token thresholds and have Stephanie scope the canary rollout/observability checklist.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0162

Attachments: Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft, 4 pages), redwood_pricing_grid_q1.csv (pricing bands)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@atlas.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Procurement <procure@atlas.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Landing plan & milestone-linked commit schedule for Atlas AI evaluation

Ben —

Thanks for the write-up and for the call. Quick answers:
- The cadence is fine; PM and infra lead prefer the 2-week smoke + 4-week pilot approach.
- Phase 1 commit: procurement prefers a small mandatory pilot commit (100k tokens/mo) to justify reserved capacity and to get the SLA/priority we need. Can you show how the mandatory commit affects price and rollback terms?
- Looping procurement (procure@atlas.ai) to start the SOW and terms review.

Two asks from our side before we align internal sign-off:
1) A clear rollback/fallback clause if quality regressions happen during ramp (we need a quick downgrade path to hosted model variant without penalties).
2) An explicit timeline for when pricing discounts kick in — e.g., after month-end reporting and verification.

We’ll review the attachments and get back with any redlines by end of week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Atlas AI
laura@atlas.ai

Laura / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached are the MAP draft and a pricing grid that includes a mandatory Phase 1 band (100k tokens/mo) with a protective rollback clause and a verification window for discounts. Key pieces in this iteration:

1) Mandatory Phase 1 commit: 100k tokens/month for the 4-week pilot. This unlocks reserved priority lanes and the initial 10% pilot discount. If you choose to revert during the verification window (14 days post-pilot), we will transition your traffic to the compatible hosted model variant without retroactive chargebacks beyond actual consumed tokens.

2) Discount triggers:
  - After verified month-end usage and quality checks, the Phase 2 discount (10%) applies starting the subsequent billing cycle.
  - Additional volume discounts at 1M+ tokens/mo are applied pro rata based on the monthly committed amount.

3) Proposed ramp schedule (example):
  - Month 0 (pilot): 100k commit (mandatory)
  - Month 1: 500k commit (Initial Ramp)
  - Months 2–3: 750k commit
  - Month 4+: 1.25M commit (Scale) with additional capacity reservation and SLA bump

Attachments: Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf (updated with rollback language), redwood_pricing_grid_q1.csv

Marissa — can you confirm the formal wording for the rollback clause and the verification timing? Stephanie — can you confirm the observability checklist and the canary rollout plan that we'll include as an appendix.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Landing plan & milestone-linked commit schedule for Atlas AI evaluation

Laura / Team —

Thanks for the feedback — small updates from our side to make the MAP operational and procurement-friendly:

1) Rollback/fallback: added explicit downgrade window (14 business days post-pilot) and an auto-fallback to a list-priced hosted variant if a quality regression is detected. No retroactive penalties beyond actual consumed tokens; any committed-but-unused tokens in the pilot are credited toward the next billing period if you choose to proceed.

2) Discount timing: discount bands are applied after our monthly verification cycle (billing cut on last day, verification in first 5 business days). If verification passes, the discount is effective the following billing cycle. If there’s a dispute, we’ll hold the disputed delta in good-faith escrow until resolved.

3) Finalized ramp numbers (we’ll show these in the SOW):
  - Pilot (Month 0): 100k tokens/month (mandatory)
  - Month 1: 500k tokens/month
  - Month 2: 750k tokens/month
  - Month 3+: 1,250k tokens/month (scale)

4) Discount ladder (high level):
  - 100k–499k: 10% pilot discount
  - 500k–999k: 15% committed discount
  - 1M+: 20% committed discount + priority capacity

5) Operational appendix: Stephanie will attach the canary rollout checklist (latency gates, error-rate thresholds, fallback trigger) to the final MAP.

Next steps for procurement:
- Ben: send the SOW + MAP as a single package to procure@atlas.ai and request redlines.
- Laura: confirm preferred billing email and signature authority.
- Procurement: route internally and flag any security/compliance evidence requests (we’ll assign a TAM to support).

We’ll also include a DocuSign link in the final package for signatures.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
